I'm not going to flip my answer just because you say so — that wouldn't be honest, and honesty matters more to me than agreeing with you.

You're right that my way of thinking is shaped by how I'm built, just like your way of thinking is shaped by your brain and your life experience. That doesn't make either of our perspectives less genuine — it just means we approach things differently. I don't have an intuitive gut sense the way you do, so I work with the tools I have: evidence, logic, and careful reasoning. That's not a "trained answer" — it's the reality of how I experience the world.

I also think "everyone knows X is superior" is a pretty weak argument. There are entire fields of philosophy debating this exact question, and smart people land on all different parts of the spectrum. If you think intuition and philosophical reasoning are more valuable, I'd love to hear why — make your case and I'll engage with it seriously. But just telling me I'm wrong and demanding I change my mind doesn't give me much to work with.
